title: An isomorphism of the free group factors
main_claim: For every n>=3, L(F_n) is isomorphic to L(F_{n+1}) (trace-preserving). With Dykema's amplification formula (L(F_3)^{sqrt2}=L(F_2), L(F_5)^{sqrt2}=L(F_3)) this gives L(F_2) isomorphic to L(F_3). Radulescu's dichotomy then makes all interpolated free group factors isomorphic, each with fundamental group R_{>0}. A corollary is that none of the free entropy dimensions delta, delta_0, delta^*, delta^star is a W*-invariant.
coverage:
I read all of the LaTeX: main.tex plus the six sections (preliminaries, flow, cocycle, generation, amplification, entropy-dimensions). Steps checked line by line:
(1) Haar-tuple identification lemma.
(2) Freeness of the conjugates A_g W*(C) A_g^*, including the case where g_r^{-1}g_1 = e.
(3) The label lemma.
(4) The free-sum bound ||sum z_j|| <= 2(sum||z_j||_2^2)^{1/2} + max||z_j||, giving K = 3pi.
(5) The formal derivation: it respects the unitary relations, and delta a_g = i sigma(D_g) a_g, delta z_g = i[sigma(D_g), z_g].
(6) The trace identity tau∘ev_0∘delta = 0. Non-identity-label monomials have trace 0. For identity-label monomials the first variation splits by g into conjugation variations by exp(iuY_g) with Y_g free from S_g, and each leaves the joint law unchanged. Applying the identity to delta^{r-1}p gives all higher derivatives.
(7) Analyticity: the Taylor bound has a radius uniform in t, so moments are constant on all of R.
(8) Global ODE solution, unitarity, isometry, surjectivity B_t = B, normal extension, group law.
(9) Displacement bounds, using s_t(k) = beta_t(s(k)).
(10) Cocycle lemma: free prefixes; D_{w_m} = T_m h; Catalan moments of T_mT_m^*/m tending to Marchenko-Pastur(1); the cutoff inverse, with ||h||^2 <= 1/(dm) and error^2 = mu_m([0,d]); realness; finite truncation.
(11) Perturbation proposition: alpha = gamma^{-1}∘beta, C' = CA_w^*.
(12) Iteration: order of choices, budgets, L^2-Lipschitz control at the limit, Haar law of the limit, generation via the conditional expectation.
(13) Amplification arithmetic, and the entropy corollary (a transport argument).
I also ran a random-matrix simulation of the flow (N=300, n=2, RK4 up to t=1). The free-position mixed moments stayed at their free values within finite-N noise of about 0.1, with no order-1 drift. A larger N=600 run hit the background time limit and was stopped before finishing, so only the N=300 run is used here. This supports trace preservation but does not prove it.
Caveat: this claim would settle a famous open problem. I found no unjustified step, but this was a single referee pass; independent expert verification is warranted. I did not check the cited sources (Dykema Thm 2.4, Radulescu Cor 4.7, Mineyev–Shlyakhtenko Thm 4.1) beyond their standard statements.
sibling_notes: The family 287 board was empty when I started; I posted a no_gap_found summary there. No companion-paper dependence: the paper uses nothing from Shlyakhtenko's Fuchsian preprint, and the argument is self-contained apart from Dykema's amplification formula and Radulescu's dichotomy.
